subject: Neighborhood and Urban Residential Zoning Updates
overview: The committee reviewed updated proposals for five new residential sub-districts designed to create a density gradient from low-density neighborhoods to transit-oriented urban residential areas. The discussion focused on balancing increased housing production with protections for existing single-family homeowners and the formalization of small-scale neighborhood commercial hubs.

items.title: Presentation of Residential Zoning Sub-Districts
items.summary: Innes Associates presented a third draft of the residential zoning proposal, establishing a gradient across five new sub-districts and adjusting boundaries based on previous feedback regarding neighborhood topography. The proposal caps residential building heights at three stories and transitions higher-density residential developments into mixed-use corridor districts.

items.title: Committee Review of Dimensional and Use Standards
items.summary: Councilors requested improvements to map legibility and discussed the technical requirements for transportation demand management and infill housing. The committee discussed maintaining a three-story maximum height to keep new structures consistent with the existing character of Medford's residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Protections for Non-Conforming Single-Family Homes
items.summary: The committee explored legislative language to ensure that existing single-family homes in new Urban Residential districts remain protected from unnecessary variance requirements for minor renovations. Discussion also addressed how new state laws regarding Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) would interact with these reclassified districts.

items.title: Analysis of Neighborhood Commercial Nodes
items.summary: Consultants presented a preliminary analysis of existing non-conforming commercial uses to identify opportunities for small-scale 'neighborhood hubs' such as bakeries and convenience stores. The committee expressed support for formalizing these nodes to enhance neighborhood walkability and community gathering spaces.

items.title: Public Participation and Housing Affordability Debate
items.summary: Residents provided testimony regarding the impact of transit-oriented density on neighborhood character and the rising cost of living, leading to a heated committee debate on whether zoning changes effectively address regional displacement. The matter was kept in committee for further review of dimensional requirements and affordability incentives.
